title: Implicit logarithmic-space computability
statement: A function $f$ from Boolean strings to Boolean strings is implicitly logarithmic-space computable if there are natural numbers $C,c$ such that $|f(x)|\le C(|x|+1)^c$ for every input $x$, and both of the following languages are in logarithmic space: the language of encodings of $(x,i)$ for which the $i$th output bit of $f(x)$ is true (taking an out-of-range bit to be false), and the language of encodings of $(x,i)$ for which $i<|f(x)|$.
hypotheses_covered: A function from Boolean strings to Boolean strings
There exist natural numbers $C,c$ bounding output length by $C(|x|+1)^c$ for every input
The indexed language testing whether the defaulted $i$th output bit is true belongs to LOGSPACE
The indexed language testing whether the index is below the output length belongs to LOGSPACE
